source_note: Read the complete actual Lamentations 1:1 preface as part of the source unit, and every unit through 2:22 in native order.
particular_checks: 1:1 matches the captivity and destruction preface with the actual 2 Kings 25 catastrophe, without replacing native names or offices.
1:14 compares ungodliness rising upon the neck with lawless deeds above the head; no yoke added.
1:16 preserves Jeremiah 38:15 as Rachel not stopping her weeping, not a refusal of comfort.
2:10 preserves Job’s friends sitting silently without adding an explicit ground location to Job 2:13.
2:13 compares rhetorical healing questions without substituting a sea-sized breach for the native cup of crushing.
2:19 links only the pouring-heart prayer language, without changing rise/exult into wailing.
2:21 preserves elders carried away in Chronicles rather than claiming that Chronicles says they were killed.
2:22 compares summoned occasions of judgment without replacing the native festival-day-of-sojourning wording.
Same-chapter 1:9 to 1:16 is supported by the joint absent-comforter and growing-enemy language.
The historically related siege, sanctuary, captivity, and famine comparisons preserve differences between narrative and personified lament.
